title: Metric geometry for ranking-based voting: Tools for learning electoral structure
abstract: arXiv:2602.10293v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: In this paper, we develop the metric geometry of ranking statistics, proving that the two major permutation distances in the statistics literature -- Kendall tau and Spearman footrule -- extend naturally to incomplete rankings with both coordinate embeddings and graph realizations. This gives us a unifying framework that allows us to connect popular topics in computational social choice: metric preferences (and metric distortion), polarization, and proportionality.   As an important application, the metric structure enables efficient identification of blocs of voters and slates of their preferred candidates. Since the definitions work for partial ballots, we can execute the methods not only on synthetic elections, but on a suite of real-world elections. translated_title: 基于排名投票的度量几何：学习选举结构的工具
translated_abstract: 在这篇论文中，我们发展了排名统计量的度量几何，证明统计学文献中两个主要的置换距离——Kendall tau（肯德尔τ）和Spearman footrule（斯皮尔曼脚距）——能够通过坐标嵌入和图实现自然地扩展到不完整排名。这提供了一个统一框架，使我们能够连接计算社会选择中的多个热门话题：度量偏好（及度量失真）、极化以及比例性。作为一个重要应用，该度量结构能够高效地识别选民集团及其偏好的候选人名单。由于这些定义适用于部分选票，我们不仅可以在合成选举上执行这些方法，还可以在一组真实世界的选举上执行。这为我们提供了稳健的聚类方法，这些方法通常产生一致的选民分组结果——即使其中一族方法基于康多塞一致的排名规则。
tldr: 本文发展了排名统计的度量几何，将Kendall tau和Spearman footrule两种置换距离自然扩展至不完整排名，建立了连接度量偏好、极化与比例性的统一框架，并能高效识别真实选举中的选民集团及其偏好候选人名单。
en_tdlr: This paper develops the metric geometry of ranking statistics by naturally extending Kendall tau and Spearman footrule distances to incomplete rankings, providing a unifying framework connecting metric preferences, polarization, and proportionality, which enables efficient identification of voter blocs and their preferred candidate slates in real-world elections.
